Welcome back! OpenAI's unreleased model went after problems that have been open since the 1950s, Claude moved into Google Docs, and an Anthropic engineer has a blunt read on what happened to code review. In today's Atlas Newsletter: Claude now edits inside your Google Docs: It reads the file you have open and edits in place, with every change behind an approval card. OpenAI dropped 722 AI-written math papers on GitHub: 4,000 open problems in, 372 result families out, and mathematicians are not uniformly thrilled. "Nobody reads the code anymore, and nothing is checking it either": Addy Osmani on the review step teams deleted and never replaced. Google shipped two models in one day: One makes images. The other runs a full multimodal RAG stack offline on your phone. PS: Want to collaborate with the biggest GTM engine and distribution moat for AI companies? You can feature your tool with us and reach millions. OpenAI dropped 722 AI-written math papers on GitHub On Tuesday night OpenAI put 722 math papers on GitHub.  A model it has never released wrote all of them. No human is listed as an author. It got handed roughly 4,000 open problems, some unanswered for over a century, with about three hours of thinking each.  What it kept became 722 papers in 372 result families. Some of the claims: A proof of the quasi-Riemann hypothesis, a weaker version of the $1M prime numbers problem Catalan's constant, studied since the 1800s, can't be written as a fraction You can't color an endless sheet of paper with five colors so that no two points an inch apart match. Open since 1950 162 papers have their main results in Lean, so a computer can check every step.  The rest don't, and OpenAI says some could contain mistakes. Last month's Navier-Stokes proof took 10,000 agents. Nearly all of these came from one prompt. Levent Alpöge, the Anthropic mathematician behind July's Jacobian result, called it the most significant moment in mathematical history.  WIRED reported anger among mathematicians hours before the drop, with some saying OpenAI had promised to space these out.  Terence Tao says problems are being harvested faster than the field can absorb them. The nine mathematicians OpenAI consults asked labs last week to stop testing models on open problems.  This week they clarified that their role is not an endorsement.
